acceptance: Dependency admission precedes CAS implementation: crates/kernux-store/Cargo.toml pins sha2 = 0.11.0 exactly with default features disabled and no optional features; third_party/dependencies/approved.json records the exact runtime purpose and MIT OR Apache-2.0 exception evidence; dependency validation passes; direct admission introduces no new external package version; and no CAS semantics land before dependency post-merge qualification.

ArtifactCas uses exactly the deterministic digest-derived layout root/sha256/xx/64hex, rejects invalid root/entry types within the bounded API, never accepts caller-controlled blob-relative path components, and exposes no public mutable-final-path primitive.

Every ingest API requires an explicit maximum size, streams through a bounded fixed buffer, accepts valid empty content, rejects over-limit input without final publication, computes exact SHA-256 and size, and rejects supplied expected-digest mismatch before publication.

Final publication is no-overwrite and fail-closed: temporary bytes are synced before publication; an existing final path is never replaced; identical existing content verifies and succeeds without revealing dedup status; corrupt/mismatched/non-regular existing content fails; ordinary failure/success removes the current temp name.

open_verified enforces an explicit byte bound, verifies the entire same read-only file handle against the requested digest before returning it, rewinds that same handle, and rejects missing, oversized, non-regular, truncated, or tampered content with typed generic errors that do not embed payload bytes or filesystem paths.

Binding CAS content to Artifact metadata requires exact expected revision, preserves existing media_type and retention_ref, writes the verified digest/size through existing invariants only after blob publication, never creates metadata referring to absent/unverified bytes, and leaves any immutable orphan blob untouched if metadata CAS fails.

Multiple logical Artifact IDs may reference one identical content digest without merging logical identity, revision, metadata, retention_ref, provenance, or authority. CAS code does not evaluate retention policy and provides no final blob deletion/GC API.

Adversarial fixtures cover exact layout, empty/multi-chunk/boundary streams, over-limit rejection, expected mismatch, identical dedup, corrupt preexisting blob, no-overwrite behavior, temp cleanup, non-regular entry rejection, tamper/truncation detection, metadata conflict/invariance, independent retention metadata, and close/reopen verification.

SQLite schema/version remains unchanged and ordinary SQLite rows contain metadata/reference fields only; KRP/generated contracts, authentication/transport, identity semantics, Event semantics, policy, secret-provider, daemon configuration, and later P02 surfaces remain unchanged.
Local macOS, Ubuntu Rust CI, and native Windows kernux-store CI execute the CAS corpus successfully. Native Windows runtime evidence is required; cross-compilation is not a substitute.

Every bounded candidate passes git diff --check, full pnpm check, dependency/provenance validation where applicable, Diffcipline R3, Alibaba OpenCodeReview Delegation Mode with complete manual accounting for exclusions, all five protected exact-head checks plus Windows kernuxd, exact-head review, zero unresolved threads, ordinary merge, and exact post-merge six-job qualification before dependent work begins.

After native SpecGrain verification and protected closeout merge/post-merge qualification, KX-P02-S04-T01 becomes PROVEN; only KX-P02-S05-T01 may become NEXT if canonical live truth still confirms it, KX-P02-S05-T02/S06 remain PLANNED, progress becomes 5/9, and P02 phase exit remains unproven.

minimality.rationale: Reuse the existing kernux-store Artifact metadata boundary and the exact sha2 0.11.0 version already present in the locked graph through ed25519-dalek. Add only the direct sha2 edge needed to call the hash API. Use std::fs/std::io for bounded filesystem streaming and publication; do not add another crate, async runtime, hex package, temp-file package, storage framework, or object-store abstraction.

requirements: Final digest paths are immutable: no accepted operation may overwrite, truncate, replace, silently repair, or delete an existing published blob.
CAS paths after the trusted root are digest-derived only. Do not accept arbitrary relative path components or wire the CAS root to untrusted KRP/renderer/browser/model/remote input in S04.
Every ingest/read is explicitly byte-bounded and streaming uses a fixed-size buffer; no API may allocate or accumulate an unbounded Artifact based on input size.
Digest verification is machine-computed over bytes. Caller/model claims, filenames, Artifact IDs, metadata size/media fields, or prior digest text do not substitute for hashing the relevant bytes.

SHA-256 digests are byte identities, not authorization tokens and not automatically non-sensitive. Do not add logs/errors or dedup-hit results that unnecessarily expose content existence or payload/path data.

Blob publication precedes metadata binding. Metadata must never be advanced to a digest/size whose final blob was not successfully published and verified; a metadata conflict leaves the immutable blob rather than deleting it as rollback.
Retention references remain metadata only. S04 must not infer deletion authority or remove final blobs; reference-aware GC/deletion remains separately governed later work.

Do not claim encryption at rest, crash-power-loss durability beyond evidence actually executed, hardened arbitrary host path authorization, cross-project authorization, or secret-safe storage beyond the explicit S04 boundaries.

outcome: Extend repository-owned kernux-store with a filesystem-backed SHA-256 content-addressed artifact store that performs bounded streaming ingest/read, verifies immutable byte identity, publishes blobs without overwrite, safely deduplicates identical content, and binds digest/size to existing Artifact metadata while preserving logical Artifact identity and deferring policy, deletion/GC, secrets, export, and daemon state-root wiring.
rationale: KX-P02-S03-T01 is PROVEN and post-merge-qualified, making KX-P02-S04-T01 the only authorized frontier. Canonical architecture separates SQLite metadata from a filesystem CAS keyed by SHA-256, P01 freezes Artifact ID versus digest semantics, and the existing kernux-store Artifact metadata already provides the correct logical binding. Reuse that crate and the exact sha2 version already present transitively rather than introducing another storage framework or crate.

risk.recovery: Revert only bounded SG-000022 refinement/implementation/closeout changes, remove the direct sha2 approval/manifest edge if introduced solely by S04, and keep KX-P02-S04-T01 at NEXT. Never delete, rewrite, repair, or mutate a previously published final digest blob as rollback automation; preserve any user bytes for explicit later lifecycle handling. Do not downgrade SG-000021 metadata schema or its proof.

scope_in: Extend crates/kernux-store with a dedicated cas module for filesystem Artifact bytes while keeping SQLite artifact metadata and blob bytes physically separate. Do not create a second storage crate or generic storage framework.

Before CAS semantics, separately admit sha2 = 0.11.0 as an exact direct runtime dependency with default-features = false and no optional features. Reuse the version already resolved transitively in Cargo.lock, document its MIT OR Apache-2.0 license exception, exact feature graph, and prove no new external package version is introduced by direct admission.

Define ArtifactCas over a caller-selected trusted local root. The root is not sourced from KRP, renderer, browser, model, or remote input in this task. Reject empty roots, non-directory roots, and symbolic-link roots where the platform exposes them; all blob/shard names are derived only from validated lowercase SHA-256 digests, never caller path segments.

Use deterministic filesystem layout <root>/sha256/<first-two-lowercase-hex>/<full-64-lowercase-hex-digest>. Final blob filenames are immutable content identities. The public API must not expose a writable final-blob handle or an arbitrary relative path join primitive.

Implement bounded streaming ingest using a fixed-size buffer and an explicit caller-supplied maximum byte count no larger than the existing SQLite Artifact size domain. Empty blobs are valid. Reading beyond the bound fails before publication and cleans the current temporary file; there is no unbounded ingest entry point.

Compute SHA-256 incrementally during ingest and return a CasBlob descriptor containing the exact Sha256Digest and size only after the stream completes successfully. When an expected digest is supplied, a mismatch fails before publication. Digest bytes are encoded as exact lowercase 64-hex using repository-owned code; do not add a hex dependency.

Publish only from a create-new temporary file in the destination shard after flush/sync_all, using same-filesystem atomic create semantics that cannot overwrite an existing final digest path. Prefer hard-link publication so an existing destination is never replaced on Unix or Windows. Remove the temporary name after successful publication or ordinary failure.

If the final digest path already exists, verify that existing regular-file bytes and size exactly match the computed digest/size before treating the ingest as successful deduplication. A missing/mismatched/corrupt/non-regular existing entry fails closed; never overwrite, replace, repair, truncate, or silently quarantine the final blob. The public result does not disclose whether deduplication occurred.

Implement bounded verified read as open_verified(digest, max_bytes): open the exact digest-derived regular file read-only, enforce the byte bound, hash the complete same file handle, compare with the requested digest, seek the same handle back to offset zero, and only then return a readable VerifiedBlob descriptor with exact size. Missing, oversized, non-regular, truncated, or digest-mismatched blobs fail with typed non-secret errors.

Bind a published CasBlob to an existing logical Artifact through the existing kernux-store revision CAS rules: require Artifact ID plus expected revision, set exact digest and size while preserving media_type and retention_ref, and preserve existing digest/size invariants. Filesystem publication occurs before metadata binding; a metadata conflict may leave an unreferenced immutable blob but must never create metadata pointing to absent/unverified bytes or delete a preexisting blob as rollback.

Prove deduplication does not merge logical Artifact identity: two Artifact IDs may bind the same content digest while preserving independent revisions, provenance-owned metadata, media metadata, and retention_ref values. The CAS does not interpret retention_ref or make retention decisions.

Prove normal ingest failures remove their current temporary file, final names are either absent or complete, and reopen after process-local close can verify/read previously published blobs. Crash-left temporary names are non-authoritative and must never be mistaken for final blobs; general stale-temp cleanup/GC is deferred.

Extend the existing kernux-store test corpus with adversarial coverage for exact layout, empty content, multi-chunk content, boundary size, over-limit streams, expected-digest mismatch, existing-identical dedup, corrupt-existing destination, final non-overwrite, temp cleanup, non-regular entries, tampered/truncated blobs, metadata binding conflicts, independent retention metadata, and reopen verification.

Use the existing Ubuntu Rust workspace job and existing native Windows kernux-store coverage without renaming protected contexts. Local macOS, Ubuntu CI, and native Windows CI must execute the CAS corpus; cross-compilation is not a substitute for Windows runtime evidence.

Keep KRP/generated contracts, T02 authentication/local transport, SG-000020 identity, SG-000021 SQLite schema version, Event semantics, policy/grants, secret providers, daemon state-root wiring, runtime-host filesystem authority, and remote/cloud behavior unchanged.

Split implementation into dependency admission followed by bounded CAS implementation/adversarial slices as required by Diffcipline R3, then native proof/closeout. Every dependent slice requires exact-head and post-merge qualification before the next begins.

After native verification and protected closeout, mark only KX-P02-S04-T01 PROVEN and advance only KX-P02-S05-T01 to NEXT if live canonical truth still confirms that dependency-ordered frontier. Keep KX-P02-S05-T02 and all S06 tasks PLANNED; P02 phase exit remains unproven.
scope_out: Do not implement reference-aware garbage collection, logical Artifact deletion, blob deletion, quota enforcement, largest-artifact UI, stale crash-temp sweeping, retention expiry execution, backup/export/import/checkpoint bundles, or deletion-integrity workflows. Later lifecycle/export work owns those behaviors.

Do not implement policy evaluation, Grant matching/admission, expiry/revocation/use accounting, permission profiles, consequence classification, delegation enforcement, or cross-project authorization. S05 owns policy; this CAS remains an internal primitive not wired directly to untrusted clients.

Do not store secret plaintext, credentials, private keys, tokens, cookies, or provider secrets in Artifact metadata or CAS-specific metadata. Do not implement Keychain, DPAPI/Credential Manager, libsecret, TPM/HSM, SQLCipher, per-blob encryption, or claim CAS encryption at rest; S06 and later encrypted modes own those semantics.

Do not accept arbitrary destination filenames/relative paths, recursively import a caller filesystem path, expose direct renderer/KRP/browser/model filesystem access, or implement a hardened general-purpose host path resolver. Runtime-host path authorization is later work; S04 only uses a trusted local CAS root and digest-derived internal names.
Do not change the SQLite schema/version or add blob bytes to SQLite. Do not put large Artifact payloads into relational rows.

Do not add async runtimes, hashing frameworks beyond exact sha2, mmap, compression, archive formats, content-defined chunking, multi-hash support, cloud/object-store backends, remote replication, filesystem watchers, or a generic virtual filesystem abstraction.
Do not expose whether a content digest was already present as a public dedup-hit signal, and do not claim SHA-256 digests are non-sensitive or authorization tokens.
title: KX-P02-S04-T01 — Establish SHA-256 artifact content-addressed store
